chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who is appointed guardian over an orphan's wealth, can he borrow from it? He said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to borrow from the wealth of orphans who were in his guardianship, so there is no problem with that.'
ai.seo_question: Can a guardian borrow money from the wealth of the orphans he manages?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of a guardian borrowing from an orphan's wealth, citing the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) as a definitive precedent. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a key evidence for the flexibility of guardianship (*wilayah*) regarding financial management, provided the borrowing does not constitute misappropriation or harm to the orphan's interests. The narration underscores that the guardian's personal use of funds is valid as long as it is done with the intent of preservation or benefit, reflecting the practical wisdom of the Imams in managing waqf-like assets.
